taxonomy.note: Accepted species, but current evidence does not meet the project's three-target-county native threshold.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts M. parvifolia and gives a native range of southeastern California to southwestern Arizona, southwestern Texas, and northern Mexico.
FNA states the eastern population is restricted to the Big Bend region of Texas and adjacent Coahuila and notes that Texas records are few.
The project source pool has one wild iNaturalist observation but no Hays/target-county source flag; unknown observation location is not counted.
No explicit records were located in searched project target counties. Explicit Big Bend records are outside the project's target zone.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: No documented project-target counties; explicit Texas evidence is centered in Big Bend/SW Texas outside the target zone.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy names are counted only where taxonomic concept is reconciled.

morphology.look_here_first: Think tiny desert milkvine: a wiry drought-deciduous twiner with leaves only about 0.5–2 cm long and tiny brown/maroon-to-green flowers with 2–3 mm triangular lobes.
diagnostic_traits: 5–9 cm narrow follicle nearly smooth to sparsely tuberculate

confusers.separator: M. sagittifolia has consistently green flowers with longer oblong-spatulate lobes and a white lobed style apex; M. parvifolia has tiny deltate lobes in brown/maroon-to-green shades and a green-to-maroon pentagonal style apex.
C. biflora is a low very hairy central-Texas herb with larger leaves and paired dark flowers; M. parvifolia is a wiry desert twiner with minute leaves and flowers.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a target-zone native unless Calvin explicitly overrides the range FAIL.
